figures.caption: Figure 1: The t-SNE visualization of multimodal features (top) and downstream performance of different methods (bottom). (a) Original CLIP: image and text embeddings form separated islands. (b) MeanCenteringLiang et al. [2022], Li et al. [2025], An et al. [2025], Yamashita et al. [2025]: centroids overlap but distributional mismatch persists. (c) Our alignment method (TPC-CMA, αtarget=0.5): true semantic interleaving. Each panel reports the Modality Gap, defined as the residual cosine distance after centroid alignment (see Section 2.2); lower values indicate better structural alignment. Bottom: downstream impact on two zero-shot tasks. (d) Image captioning CIDEr improves from 0.210 to 0.330. (e) Joint clustering ARI improves from 0.318 to 0.516.

Figure 4: Gap vs. Accuracy Pareto Frontier. TPCCMA forms a smooth efficient frontier that envelopes all selected baselines. AlignCLIP and M2Mix fall significantly below the frontier, while CLIPRefine fails to reduce the gap.
Table 3: Joint image-text clustering following Grassucci et al. Grassucci et al. [2026] (ImageNet val, 200 classes × 50 imgs, KMeans k=200).
Table 1: Main comparison across gap reduction, discriminative, generative, and structural tasks.

Figure 2: Overview of TPC-CMA. A: CLIP backbone extracts image and text embeddings. B: CMA Loss combines Negative Reweighting (reduces Centroid Gap) and Intra-modal Geometry Matching (reduces Distribution Gap) via α. C: Three-Phase Curriculum schedules α from 0 to αtarget across Anchor, Gradient-aware Ramp-up, and Stabilize stages, with the transition speed dynamically modulated by the observed gradient dynamics between loss terms.
